title: arXiv Trending Physics — Friday, 20 November 2026
global_caveat: arXiv publishes no official trending chart. This is an inferred notable-paper selection based on concrete results, cross-listing, dataset and publication/release signals; the papers are very recent and citation/attention evidence is limited, so this is not a popularity ranking.

sections.title: First $\Omega_{\rm m}-w$ Measurement Using Only Fast Radio Burst Observations
sections.abstract: The authors combine a cosmology-dependent matter-spectrum emulator and electron model to infer Ωm and w from dispersion measures of 125 localized FRBs, obtaining broad FRB-only constraints and a positive parameter degeneracy.
sections.claimed_result: The authors infer Ωm=0.33(+0.10/-0.11) and w=-0.80(+0.28/-0.38) in flat wCDM, with an Ωm–w degeneracy opposite to that from Type Ia supernovae.
sections.evidence_type: observational; likelihood analysis of 125 localized FRBs at 0.105≤z≤2.148 using an emulator-based model for cosmic dispersion-measure mean and variance
sections.unique_caveat: The authors say the broad posterior extends beyond the emulator’s validated training range; the electron model fixes feedback-related calibrations, and the fit also adopts a BBN prior and fixed primordial-spectrum and neutrino parameters.

sections.title: FAST Burst-Cluster Catalog of FRB 20240114A
sections.abstract: The authors present a catalog of 13,261 burst clusters, 19,037 bursts, and 29,026 sub-bursts from a 495-day FAST monitoring campaign, reporting temporal and spectral patterns including a rising dispersion measure.
sections.claimed_result: The authors report a manually refined DM increase of 1.29±0.11 pc cm−3 yr−1, downward-to-upward sub-burst drift of about 9.4:1, and inter-cluster intervals broadly consistent with a rate-variable Poisson process.
sections.evidence_type: observational; FAST L-band observations over 99 sessions (58.83 hours), with burst and cluster identification and statistical analysis
sections.unique_caveat: This is one repeating source, and the authors note substantial scatter in energy-related trends; the catalog’s clustering and manual DM refinement are analysis choices that should be compared across sources and methods.

sections.title: Every galaxy is a radio source: a stellar-mass dependent minimum 150 MHz luminosity identified in the LoTSS Deep Fields
sections.abstract: Using LoTSS Deep Fields radio data and Prospector-derived properties for 113,228 galaxies, the authors find a stellar-mass-dependent minimum radio luminosity and argue that weak accretion can contribute to radio emission otherwise attributed to star formation.
sections.claimed_result: The authors report a mass-dependent lower envelope in 150 MHz luminosity, especially for low-specific-SFR galaxies, and find that a star-formation plus weak-AGN model reproduces the observed trends.
sections.evidence_type: observational; 150 MHz LoTSS Deep Fields DR2 and SFR/mass estimates for 113,228 near-infrared-selected galaxies, modeled with Prospector-based properties
sections.unique_caveat: The weak-AGN explanation is an interpretation supported by a two-component model, not a direct identification of accretion in every galaxy; the inference also depends on the sample and estimated galaxy properties.

sections.title: Local velocimetry for atomic superfluids: from Riemann rarefaction waves to quantized vortices
sections.abstract: The authors use Raman–Bragg matter-wave interferometry to reconstruct a two-dimensional atomic-superfluid velocity field, demonstrating the method on rarefaction flow and quantized vortices.
sections.claimed_result: The authors map the wavefunction phase gradient to interference-fringe displacement and report direct reconstruction of the 2D velocity field, including quantized circulation around vortices.
sections.evidence_type: experimental; Raman–Bragg matter-wave interferometry on a two-dimensional atomic superfluid
sections.unique_caveat: The abstract demonstrates the method on two canonical examples; broader validation across flow regimes and geometries remains to be established.

sections.title: Measurements of inclusive J/ψ production in Au+Au collisions at √sNN = 14.6, 17.3, 19.6, and 27 GeV with the STAR experiment
sections.abstract: The STAR Collaboration measures inclusive mid-rapidity J/ψ production at four RHIC collision energies and reports centrality and transverse-momentum trends in the nuclear modification factor.
sections.claimed_result: The authors report RAA near 0.5 for the 0–20% centrality class and a tendency for RAA to rise with pT at 14.6–27 GeV; the central-collision yield shows no significant variation within uncertainties across 14.6–200 GeV.
sections.evidence_type: experimental; STAR detector measurements of Au+Au collisions at the Relativistic Heavy Ion Collider, compared with an interpolated p+p reference
sections.unique_caveat: The paper describes the centrality dependence as a hint and the low-energy pT behavior as a tendency; interpretation depends on the reference and competing hot- and cold-nuclear-matter effects.

sections.title: Star-forming disc galaxies align tangentially with the cosmic tidal field
sections.abstract: Combining SPHEREx spectrophotometry and DESI Legacy Imaging Surveys, the authors report tangential alignment of blue disc galaxies and radial alignment of red spheroids in a 71-million-galaxy catalog.
sections.claimed_result: The authors report tangential alignment of blue discs at 22.5σ and radial alignment of red spheroids at 65σ; their density-environment tests favor a linear response to the cosmic tidal field over the classic purely quadratic tidal-torque picture.
sections.evidence_type: observational; full-sky galaxy catalog combining SPHEREx spectrophotometry with DESI Legacy Imaging Surveys
sections.unique_caveat: The measured alignments are not by themselves a causal account of galaxy formation; their interpretation and impact on lensing depend on sample selection and modeling of intrinsic alignments.

sections.title: Nonlinearly Causal General-Relativistic Superfluid Hydrodynamics: Simulating Vortex Dynamics in Neutron-Star Interiors
sections.abstract: The authors develop a nonlinear-causal general-relativistic superfluid framework with vortex dynamics, derive well-posedness conditions, and construct a finite-volume scheme tested on relativistic-flow and neutron-star calculations.
sections.claimed_result: The authors derive necessary and sufficient conditions for nonlinear causality and strong hyperbolicity, identify short-wavelength ill-posedness in common no-line-tension formulations, and demonstrate stable evolution with a new finite-volume scheme.
sections.evidence_type: theoretical and computational; analytic conditions, exact/dispersion-relation tests, and general-relativistic two-fluid neutron-star simulations
sections.unique_caveat: The spin-down calculation prescribes vortex release and repinning, so it is a framework demonstration rather than a self-consistent prediction of observed pulsar glitches.

sections.title: Which black hole modes ring freely? Horizon regularity, the forced ringdown transient, and GW250114
sections.abstract: The authors derive horizon-regularity conditions for outgoing perturbations and compare a horizon-mode ringdown model with a conventional overtone fit to GW250114.
sections.claimed_result: For a scalar-like perturbation, the authors derive a ladder of horizon-mode frequencies and report Bayes factors of 2–30 favoring a fundamental-plus-first-horizon-mode fit over a fundamental-plus-first-overtone fit in the analyzed time range.
sections.evidence_type: theoretical and observational; horizon-regularity analysis, GW250114 ringdown fits, and zero-noise injections of numerical-relativity-calibrated waveforms
sections.unique_caveat: The reported model preference is modest and model-dependent; the inferred remnant shift is interpreted by the authors as nonlinear backreaction, not as an independent detection of a new mode or a consensus result.
